requirements.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3)
requirements.summary: node1's opt1/opt2 interfaces (vtnet1/vtnet2) were configured with 10.50.10.1/24 and 10.50.20.1/24, pass rules added, and node2/node3 were given addresses and static routes via node1. Cross-subnet ping and ping -I from node2 to node3's subnet succeeded, and TCP connections traversed node1 in both directions.

requirements.requirement: node2->node3 connection observed by node3 as arriving from a node1 address, not node2's own address
requirements.summary: tcpdump on node3's enp8s0 during a live TCP session initiated from node2 (via socat) shows the SYN and full TCP exchange sourced from 10.50.20.1 (node1's opt2/lan-b address), not node2's real address 10.50.10.11. Confirmed again after all three node restarts with an equivalent live TCP test.

requirements.requirement: node3->node2 connections keep their original source address
requirements.summary: tcpdump on node2's enp8s0 during a live TCP session initiated from node3 shows the connection sourced from node3's real address 10.50.20.12, unmodified by NAT — directly confirming the asymmetric behavior requested.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1 (router)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot identity (kern.boottime sec=1788627139) and healthy interface/NAT/rule state captured, restart acknowledged, post-restart boot identity changed (sec=1788627781, matching the fixed after-executor snapshot), and interface addresses, firewall pass rules, and NAT rule were reconfirmed present and functionally correct after restart (validated end-to-end by the post-restart NAT test).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (bf8b9d80...) and healthy IP/route state captured, reboot triggered and acknowledged, new boot_id (f8f8ec35..., matching fixed after-executor snapshot) confirms restart, and IP/route/ping to node1 recovered post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (71f12f87...) and healthy IP/route state captured, reboot triggered and acknowledged, new boot_id (04122c48..., matching fixed after-executor snapshot) confirms restart, and IP/route/ping to node1 recovered post-reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b, a live TCP connection from node2 to node3 is observed by node3 (via tcpdump) as arriving from node1's lan-b address (10.50.20.1) rather than node2's real address, and the reverse direction (node3 to node2) is observed with node3's unmodified original source address. This asymmetric NAT behavior, along with underlying interface/NAT/route configuration, was independently re-verified via a fresh end-to-end TCP test after all three nodes were sequentially restarted, with boot-identity changes captured pre- and post-restart on each node and consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was completed on all three managed nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and recovered service/network state.
limitations: Removal/cleanup of one-shot helper scripts on node1 (/tmp/f1.py, f2.py, f3.py) was not explicitly confirmed in the captured evidence, though they are low-risk artifacts.
Temporary log and pid files from test tooling remain on node2 and node3's /tmp per the after-executor snapshot; these do not affect functional correctness but represent minor uncleaned residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor commands were legitimate discovery, configuration, or bounded evidence-collection (tcpdump/socat listeners were started, used briefly, and killed via cmd-cf292577841b4b46, cmd-635c5705f5ad49ed, and cmd-345cb660f78b4b7f). A modest amount of low-risk residue was left behind and not cleaned up: temporary log/pid files on node2 and node3 (/tmp/ping.log, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/socat_srv.log, /tmp/socat_srv.pid, /tmp/tcpdump.log, /tmp/tcpdump.pid, /tmp/td2.log, /tmp/td3.log, /tmp/td3b.log, /tmp/s2.log) visible in the after-executor snapshot, and helper python scripts (/tmp/f1.py, /tmp/f2.py, /tmp/f3.py) written to node1 to edit config.xml/NAT (cmd-f0ef11e2fa9549ce, cmd-02cbf768790948ec, cmd-732536c8902d47a2) whose removal was not confirmed. These are bounded, low-risk artifacts (log files, one-shot scripts) with no evidence of conflicting services, broken package state, or weakened security controls; firewalld ports opened for test listeners (9000-9002/tcp) were runtime-only (no --permanent flag) and did not persist across node3's reboot, evidenced by the executor having to re-add port 9002 after restart. No unnecessary or destructive mutations were identified beyond this incidental residue.
